title: Token fingerprint dashboard - early spec
content:
Goal:
- Build a compact, scannable dashboard that surfaces token-level cost and latency 'fingerprints' for invocations so SREs, ML infra, and product engineers can quickly pinpoint hot paths and regression sources.

Problem statement / user needs:
- Current per-model metrics hide per-invocation token patterns; teams need to see where cost and latency accumulate across tokens (prefix vs generation, KV cache hits, long-tail tokens).
- Operations need a signal to triage: is a spike caused by tokenization, attention compute, KV misses, or a large generated continuation?
- Product engineers want a fast way to compare model variants and rollout buckets at token-level granularity.

Primary personas:
- Platform SRE: triage latency incidents and identify if changes to routing, batching, or autoscaling are effective.
- ML Engineer: validate that quantization / compilation reduced cost without increasing tail latency on critical tokens.
- Product PM/Designer: understand UX token patterns for customer-facing flows.

High-level UX goals:
- Compact summary view (30k-ft) that lists invocations as rows with a token fingerprint sparkline.
- Expandable rows for full waterfall per-invocation with lane annotations (tokenization, prefix-KV, attention, softmax, IO).
- Fast filter and sort by cost contribution, 95/99 latency, prefix-reuse score, and KV cache hit rate.
- Anomaly markers and ability to pin examples for replay and deeper analysis.

Key concepts / terminology (for UI labels):
- Token fingerprint: condensed visualization of per-token cost/latency across an invocation.
- Token lane: color-coded band representing cost category (compute-attention, KV, tokenization, IO).
- Prefix reuse score: fraction of tokens satisfied from prefix cache.
- Dense mode vs Expanded mode: row compacted to a sparkline vs full token-by-token waterfall.

Wireframe sketch (logical layout):
- Top bar: time picker, model selector, deployment tier toggle (hosted / dedicated / private), quantization filter, batch-size slider.
- Left column: invocation list (sortable) with small metadata columns (invocation id, model, route, user tag, tokens-in, tokens-out, cost, p95, p99).
- Middle column: token fingerprint lane for each invocation (sparkline style):
  - X axis = token index over invocation (compact, fixed width).
  - Color intensity = latency contribution; small vertical bars per token show token cost.
  - Overlays: KV-hit ribbon (thin green line), cache-miss pulses (red ticks).
- Right column: quick actions and insights: pinned examples, anomaly badges, quick replay button, 'compare with variant' CTA.

Row interactions and states:
- Hover token in sparkline: tooltip shows token text (or token id), cost ms, cost $ estimate, breakdown by lane (e.g., attention 4.3ms, KV 1.1ms).
- Click row to expand: shows token waterfall with lanes stacked and timeline scrubber for playback.
- Multi-select rows: run batch compare across selected invocations (side-by-side token waterfalls).
- Pin example: store to 'investigations' panel with linked artifacts and notes.

Token waterfall detail view:
- Top: invocation metadata header (route, model + variant, quantization, batch, device, request headers).
- Middle: stacked token lanes across timeline with interactive zoom. Each token has small tooltips and clickable link to invocation raw logs.
- Bottom: diagnostics panel: suggested root causes (heuristic), related traces (SLO breaches), and automated recommendations (increase batch, enable prefix caching, switch to quantized variant).

Hypotheses we want to validate during prototype testing:
- H1: Developers can find the root cause of a p99 spike faster with token fingerprint + KV ribbon than with per-request timelines alone.
- H2: Compact fingerprint rows reduce cognitive load for scanning heavy traffic by 30% (measured by time to first actionable insight).
- H3: Pinning and batch compare flows are the primary adoption path for infra teams investigating regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- MVP displays token fingerprints for at least 5000 recent invocations and can open expanded detail for any of them within 800ms.
- Hover tooltip contains token text/id, ms, and $ cost estimate.
- Filters for model, quantization, batch size, and route function correctly and update fingerprint list within 1s.
- Ability to pin an invocation, add note, and export link to investigation.

Backlog tickets / grooming notes (rough):
- CON-411: data pipeline: emit per-token cost attribution with lane tags (tokenization, kv, attention, other).
- CON-412: frontend: compact sparkline component + hover microtooltip design.
- CON-413: UX: expand/collapse interaction + playback scrubber.
- CON-414: infra: store 'prefix reuse score' and KV-hit timeline in trace events.
- CON-415: analytics: compute aggregated token-level percentiles for model variants.

Design tradeoffs discussed:
- Privacy: showing token text may leak PII. Default to token id only; provide opt-in to reveal token text for whitelisted investigations.
- Sampling vs completeness: showing all tokens for very long generations can be noisy. Introduce downsampling modes: head-only, tail-only, uniform sample, and full.
- UI density: balance between showing rich per-token data vs scanability of many rows. Offer 'dense' default with quick expand.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Which lane taxonomy is stable enough for the initial rollout? (proposal: tokenization, KV, attention, softmax/other).
- How to attribute multi-step tool calls that embed multiple model invocations? Should we show nested fingerpints?
- Pricing signal: show dollar amounts per-token in all tiers or hide for developer plans?

Next steps (this sprint):
- Sync with serving-runtime on CON-411 to finalize telemetry schema (Rohan + infra).
- Quick prototype: React sparkline + fake data generator (Evelyn) for usability sessions.
- Usability test plan: 6 participants across SRE and ML eng, tasks include triage of 3 incident types.
- Draft copy for privacy modal and opt-in flow.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- 'Fingerprint compare' overlay: take two invocations and compute diff heatmap to highlight token-level deltas.
- Idea: show 'token instability' metric across time windows to flag model outputs that vary a lot per same prefix.
- Consider keyboard navigation for power users (next/prev invocation, expand, pin).

References and related docs:
- CON-311: token-sleuth heuristics (related heuristics doc)
- link: product/console/atomic-token-breakdown-scenarios (internal)

Sketch artifacts: attach later - will include simple SVG wireframes for the dense row vs expanded row patterns.

Status and ownership:
- Owner: Ava Martinez (product).
- Engineering leads: Rohan Patel (frontend), Karim Nasr (infra), Evelyn Cho (ux).

----
End of early-spec. This is intentionally rough — use as input for grooming; prefer short, testable tickets rather than more prose.
